claims.claim: Metamorphic rocks began as igneous, sedimentary, or earlier metamorphic rocks and are substantially changed by high heat, pressure, mineral-rich fluids, or combinations of these conditions.
Metamorphism transforms rock while it remains solid; if rock melts, it becomes magma and later cooling forms igneous rock.
During metamorphism, original minerals can be replaced atom by atom by new minerals through rearrangement of components or reactions involving fluids.
Foliation forms when directed pressure aligns flat or elongate minerals, creating a planar fabric that reflects pressure direction.
Not all metamorphic rocks are foliated because parent rocks may lack platy or elongate minerals; nonfoliated rocks can form through several histories including local contact metamorphism.
Regional metamorphism affects broad areas and is commonly related to tectonic burial and mountain building, while contact metamorphism is local thermal alteration near magma.
Metamorphic rocks are classified using texture and mineral composition, and precise interpretations may require field relationships and laboratory evidence beyond a hand sample.
